title: AC-MT202-AnchorModel

scope.summary:
GOAL: Define the typed multi-selector anchor model `AnnotationAnchor` that makes annotations survive file edits: Hypothesis-style redundant selectors (position + exact quote + prefix/suffix context) over a Gerrit-style path/side/range base, with a content hash for the unchanged fast path. This MT replaces the MT-201 opaque AnchorRef payload with the typed model while keeping serialization stable. NEVER diff-relative offsets (GitHub's legacy `position` field is deprecated for exactly this fragility — the REJECTED design).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) new file src/backend/handshake_core/src/annotations/anchor.rs with the anchor types + construction helpers; (b) record.rs edit swapping the AnchorRef envelope payload from serde_json::Value to AnnotationAnchor (envelope shape unchanged: anchor_version stays the outer discriminator); (c) mod.rs re-exports; (d) unit tests. NO persistence, NO re-anchoring logic (MT-204), NO fuzzy-match crate added here.

DETAILED SPEC — struct `AnnotationAnchor` (serde, deny_unknown_fields):
1. `path: String` — workspace-relative, forward slashes (document the normalization rule; reject absolute paths and `..` traversal with a typed error).
2. `side: AnchorSide` — enum old | new | live_file (serde lowercase). `old`/`new` are the two sides of a diff subject (Gerrit PARENT/REVISION mapped to Handshake's DiffMode old/new panes — see diff_editor_panel.rs DiffMode SideBySide/Inline/Merge); `live_file` anchors to the current working-copy content of a File subject.
3. `line_range: LineRange { start: u32, end: u32 }` — 0-based, HALF-OPEN [start, end), matching the native diff engine's `DiffBlock { left_lines/right_lines: Range<usize> }` convention (diff_engine.rs) so hunk-selection construction is a direct copy, no off-by-one conversion. end > start required (typed error); end == start is invalid (an anchor always covers at least one line).
4. `char_range: Option<CharRange { start_line_byte: u32, end_line_byte: u32 }>` — optional sub-line precision: UTF-8 byte offset within the FIRST line (start) and within the LAST line (end). Byte offsets must fall on char boundaries at construction time (typed error otherwise).
5. `quote: String` — the exact text of the anchored region at anchor-creation time, truncated to 4 KiB max (if truncated, `quote_truncated: bool` is set and content_hash still covers the FULL region).
6. `context: AnchorContext { prefix: String, suffix: String }` — up to 256 bytes of exact text immediately before/after the anchored region (Hypothesis TextQuoteSelector prefix/suffix), empty at file boundaries.
7. `hunk_header: Option<String>` — the `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` header of the enclosing hunk when the anchor was made from a diff selection; None for live_file anchors. Informational/display only — NEVER used for resolution (that would reintroduce diff-relative fragility).
8. `content_hash: String` — lowercase hex SHA-256 of the FULL anchored region bytes (before quote truncation). Use the hashing crate already in the handshake_core dependency tree (verify: grep sha2/blake3 in Cargo.toml; prefer the incumbent; if none exists, add sha2 as the boring field-standard choice and record it).
9. `anchor_version: u32` — always 1 in this MT; the outer envelope discriminator from MT-201 continues to carry it.
10. Construction helpers (pure functions, no I/O):
    a. `AnnotationAnchor::from_diff_selection(path, side, hunk_header, full_side_text: &str, line_range) -> Result<Self, AnchorError>` — given the FULL text of one side of a diff and a selected line range, extracts quote/context/hash. Caller (diff GUI or tool surface) supplies the side text; this crate does not read files.
    b. `AnnotationAnchor::from_live_selection(path, full_file_text: &str, line_range, char_range) -> Result<Self, AnchorError>` — same for a live-file selection; side = live_file.
    c. `AnnotationAnchor::resolve_exact(&self, current_text: &str) -> ExactResolution` — the CHEAP resolution primitive MT-204 builds on: enum Match (region at recorded position hashes to content_hash) | MovedCandidate (hash mismatch at position; NOT a search — just the typed signal) | RangeOutOfBounds. No fuzzy logic here.
11. `AnchorError` typed enum: PathNotWorkspaceRelative, EmptyLineRange, RangeOutOfBounds, CharOffsetNotOnBoundary, QuoteContextExtractionFailed.
12. Stable serialization: a committed golden JSON fixture test asserts the serialized anchor byte-shape (field order via serde struct order, lowercase enums) so MT-203 rows and exported sidecars never drift silently.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the MT-201 record.rs AnchorRef envelope docs and diff_engine.rs DiffBlock ranges (native-editors worktree) before writing types.
2. Implement anchor.rs types + helpers with exhaustive rustdoc, including the 'never diff-relative offsets' law and the resolution-independence of hunk_header.
3. Swap AnchorRef's payload type in record.rs; prove serialization compatibility with a fixture captured before the swap (an MT-201-era serialized annotation must still deserialize).
4. Unit tests per expected_tests; include multi-byte UTF-8 content (CJK + emoji) in quote/context/char_range tests.
5. Run proof targets; keep the module import-clean (seam law).
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml (hash crate only if none incumbent)
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (GUI owned by NA family MT-221+)
acceptance_criteria: AnnotationAnchor exists with exactly: path, side (old|new|live_file), line_range (0-based half-open), optional char_range (UTF-8 byte, boundary-validated), quote (4 KiB cap + truncation flag), context prefix/suffix (256-byte cap), optional hunk_header, content_hash (SHA-256 hex of full region), anchor_version.
No field or code path expresses a diff-relative offset; hunk_header is provably display-only (grep: hunk_header never read inside resolve_exact or any resolution helper).

from_diff_selection and from_live_selection produce correct quote/context/hash for ASCII and multi-byte UTF-8 content, at file start/end boundaries, from caller-supplied text (no file I/O in the module).
resolve_exact returns Match on unchanged content, MovedCandidate on hash mismatch at the recorded position, RangeOutOfBounds when the range exceeds current content — and performs no searching.
An MT-201-era serialized annotation (opaque-envelope fixture) still deserializes after the typed swap; the golden anchor JSON fixture pins the serialized shape.
line_range convention matches diff_engine.rs DiffBlock half-open Range semantics, asserted by a test constructing an anchor directly from a DiffBlock-shaped range.
All invalid inputs (absolute path, .., empty range, out-of-bounds, non-boundary char offset) fail with typed AnchorError variants.
cargo build + clippy clean; annotations module still imports nothing from knowledge/loom/atelier/api/storage.
proof_targets: cargo test --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml annotation_anchor -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'
grep -n 'hunk_header' src/backend/handshake_core/src/annotations/anchor.rs | grep -v '//' | grep -c 'resolve' | grep -q '^0$' (hunk_header never used in resolution)
cargo test --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml annotation_record -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok' (MT-201 suite unbroken after payload swap)
implementation_notes: Multi-selector redundancy is the Hypothesis fuzzy-anchoring design: position selector (line_range/char_range) + TextQuoteSelector (quote) + context (prefix/suffix). MT-204 consumes them in that order; this MT only records them faithfully.

Known Hypothesis failure mode motivating the caps: short generic quotes in large documents cause pathological fuzzy searches. The 4 KiB quote cap + 256-byte context cap + content_hash fast path are the recorded mitigations; MT-204 adds the bounded search window.

GROUNDING FACT: diff_engine.rs (wtc-native-editors-v1, src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/) defines DiffBlock with half-open Range<usize> line ranges built from similar v2 TextDiff::from_lines (Myers); adopting the same convention makes the GUI's hunk-selection-to-anchor construction a field-for-field copy.

AnchorSide::old/new maps to Gerrit side=PARENT/REVISION; live_file has no Gerrit equivalent (Gerrit only anchors to revisions) and exists because Handshake annotates working copies during agent steering.
Do NOT add diff-match-patch-rs or dissimilar here — the fuzzy crate selection (with recorded benchmark) is MT-204's deliverable.
Helpers take full side/file text as &str by design: the annotations crate stays I/O-free, callers (MT-205 routes, MT-206 tools, NA GUI) own content retrieval.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/core anchor model MT; operator GUI surfaces for annotations are owned by the NA family (MT-221+).

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal data-model MT with no operator-visible behavior yet; the UserManual entries land with the MT-205 routes and MT-206 tool surface.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: FlightRecorder: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason — pure anchor construction/resolution primitives emit no runtime events; MT-204 emits the re-anchor outcome events (MT-161 kinds).
internal_diagnostics: WIRED — every invalid construction input is a typed AnchorError variant; resolve_exact returns typed states, never a silent default.
Palmistry: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason — no long-running runtime posture; pure functions over caller-supplied text.
risk_if_missed: Anchors collapse to single-selector line numbers or (worse) diff-relative offsets: any upstream edit silently shifts every annotation onto the wrong code (the GitHub legacy-position failure), the MT-204 fallback chain has no quote/context selectors to fall back to, and mis-attached model feedback poisons agent-steering decisions.

risks: RISK-1: char_range recorded in chars on one path and UTF-8 bytes on another; multi-byte content (CJK/emoji) silently shifts sub-line anchors or panics on slicing.
RISK-2: hunk_header quietly becomes a resolution input (cheap-looking shortcut), reintroducing the deprecated diff-relative-offset fragility the design explicitly rejects.

RISK-3: content_hash computed over the truncated 4 KiB quote instead of the full region — large anchored regions then hash-match after edits beyond the truncation point, defeating the MT-204 fast path.
RISK-4: The record.rs payload swap breaks deserialization of any annotation serialized during MT-201 (envelope shape drift), invalidating early fixtures and any pre-MT-203 exports.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): All offsets documented and validated as UTF-8 byte offsets on char boundaries; dedicated multi-byte tests cover CJK + emoji at range edges.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Grep proof target asserts hunk_header is never referenced in resolution code; rustdoc states the display-only law.

CTRL-3 (RISK-3): A test anchors a region larger than 4 KiB, asserts quote_truncated=true, and asserts resolve_exact still matches via the full-region hash — then flips one byte beyond 4 KiB and asserts MovedCandidate.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): The MT-201-era envelope fixture is committed BEFORE the swap and must deserialize after it; the golden fixture pins the post-swap shape.

research_provenance.source: Operator-verified annotation research 2026-07-21: Gerrit CommentInfo anchor base (path + side REVISION/PARENT + line OR range{start_line,start_character,end_line,end_character}); Hypothesis fuzzy anchoring multi-selector redundancy (position selector + TextQuoteSelector exact quote + prefix/suffix context) with the documented short-generic-quote perf failure; REJECTED: diff-relative offsets (GitHub legacy position field deprecated). Grounding audit of wtc-native-editors-v1: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/diff_engine.rs (similar v2 Myers, TextDiff::from_lines, DiffBlock half-open Range<usize>, prose block-level entry point explicitly DEFERRED in mod docs lines 5-11) and diff_editor_panel.rs (DiffMode SideBySide/Inline/Merge, enum at line 74).
corrections: Gerrit ranges are 1-based end-inclusive character positions; Handshake deliberately adopts 0-based half-open line ranges + UTF-8 byte columns instead, to be identical to the native DiffBlock convention — the divergence from Gerrit is intentional and documented in rustdoc.
hunk's live-comment one-of targeting (hunk|hunkNumber|oldLine|newLine) is superseded by this multi-selector anchor; hunk_header survives only as display metadata.
